title: Why Your Home Espresso Tastes Sour (3 Fixes That Actually Work)
creator: Dana Okafor
description:
Sour shots are the number one question in my comments, so here are the three things I check every single time.

0:00 The sour shot problem
1:05 Fix one: grind finer
2:20 My setup
3:00 Fix two: temperature
4:05 Fix three: ratio and time

Gear I use (affiliate links, I earn a small commission at no cost to you):
Baratza Encore ESP grinder: https://amzn.to/3xK9pQe
Timemore Black Mirror scale: https://amzn.to/4bRt2Lm
Bottomless portafilter (58mm): https://amzn.to/3yQe7Hw

Beans in this video: a washed Ethiopian from my local roaster.

Instagram: @danapullsshots

sentences.t: Okay, so if you've ever pulled a shot and it tasted like you licked a lemon, this video is for you.
That's the sour shot, and honestly it's the most common thing people ask me about.
And the good news is it's almost always one of three things.
So let me pull one first so you can see what we're dealing with.
Look at that, see how fast it's running?
That's like fifteen seconds and it's already blonde and thin and kind of watery.
Let me taste it.
Yeah, oof, that's sour, that's really sharp at the front of the tongue.
So fix number one, and this is the big one, is grind size.
Sourness basically means under-extraction, the water ran through too fast and only grabbed the acids.
The acids come out first, then the sugars, then the bitter stuff at the end.
So if you stop too early, all you get is the acid, and that's your lemon shot.
Going finer slows the water down, so it has more time to pull out the sweet stuff.
I'm going to go about three clicks finer here, which on this grinder is a pretty big jump.
And yeah, a few people have asked what I'm actually using, so real quick.
The grinder is the Baratza Encore ESP, the scale is a Timemore, and the portafilter is just a generic bottomless one.
I've linked all three down in the description, and just so you know, those are affiliate links.
So if you buy through them I get a small commission, it doesn't cost you anything extra, and it helps the channel a bit.
Nobody's paying me to say this stuff, it's literally just what's on my counter.
You absolutely do not need this exact gear to fix a sour shot, any grinder that goes fine enough will do.
Okay, shot number two, three clicks finer, same dose, eighteen grams in.
Watch the flow now, it's way slower, it's kind of honey-looking at the start.
Twenty eight seconds, thirty six grams out, that's about where I want it.
Tasting.
Okay, so much better, there's still a little brightness but now there's this caramel thing underneath.
If yours is still sour after going finer, that brings us to fix number two, which is temperature.
A lot of machines, especially the cheaper single boiler ones, run kind of cool.
And cooler water extracts slower, so you end up under-extracted again even with a good grind.
If your machine lets you set the temperature, bump it up two or three degrees and see what happens.
If it doesn't, a trick I used for years is to run a blank shot first to heat everything up.
Just run water through the group with no coffee for a few seconds, then lock in and pull right away.
Also, light roasts are way harder here, they're denser and they just need more heat and more time.
So if you bought some fancy fruity Ethiopian and it's sour no matter what, that's partly the beans being picky.
Okay, fix number three is ratio and time, and this is the one people skip.
If you're doing a one to one ratio, like eighteen in and eighteen out, that's a ristretto, and it's going to lean sour.
Try going longer, one to two and a half, so eighteen grams in and about forty five out.
You're pushing more water through, so you're pulling more of those sugars at the tail end.
Let me show you, same grind as the good shot, I'm just going to let it run longer.
There we go, forty four grams, thirty four seconds.
And honestly with this coffee I think I like this one even more, it's rounder, it's softer.
So, quick recap, because I know I talk a lot.
Sour means under-extracted, so grind finer first, then check your temperature, then try a longer ratio.
Change one thing at a time, taste every shot, and write down what you did, even just in your phone notes.
Next week I'm doing the opposite problem, bitter shots, which is a whole other can of worms.
Let me know in the comments what machine you're on and I'll try to help you dial it in.
Alright, I'm going to go drink these, see you next week.
